newsitem.title: FRANCE: Agnelli boosts stake in Club Med - paper.
newsitem.headline: Agnelli boosts stake in Club Med - paper.

text.p: Italy's Agnelli group has boosted its stake in Club Mediterranee to just over 19 percent from 13 percent in the wake of management changes at the French holiday firm, financial daily Les Echos reported on Tuesday.

The move, carried out in recent weeks by Agnelli subsidiary Exor, strengthens Agnelli's position as the resort operator's leading shareholder but falls short of the 20 percent stake that would have triggered a public declaration, it said.
"This increase in power...was expected," Les Echos said. The Agnelli group had played a key role in selecting Euro Disney boss Philippe Bourguignon to run Club Med in February.
Club Mediterranee was not immediately available for comment.
Leading investors in the firm, which runs vacation villages worldwide, paved the way for changes in its ownership structure last December by ending a key shareholder pact.
The six-year-old agreement limited stakes among six big shareholders to 13 percent each.

Club Mediterranee announced Bourguignon's appointment in February after reporting a loss of 743 million francs for the year to October 31, 1996. Analysts said Exor, which had raised its stake a year before to 12.9 percent, had led the charge against previous head Serge Trigano, son of the group's founder.
